@NAME@ - start here
====================

@NAME@ is a karaoke app that looks like a bubbler jukebox. This folder is everything
for one USB stick: the Windows app, a place for the Mac app, your songs, and the
Studio that makes new songs on a Windows PC with an NVIDIA graphics card.

Built @DATE@. Size: about @SIZE_GB@ GB on an exFAT stick (@FILES@ files).


1. What each folder is
----------------------

  Windows\      The Windows app. Double-click Windows\@NAME@.exe to start it.
                Windows\resources\ holds the demo song the self-check uses.
                Windows\Studio\ is the Studio, the part that turns any song into a
                karaoke song. It only runs on Windows with an NVIDIA graphics card;
                on other PCs the app still plays everything and says why the Studio
                is unavailable.
  Mac\          The Mac app goes here (Mac\@NAME@.app). It could not be built on the
                Windows PC: read Mac\README.txt for how to get it.
  Library\      Your songs (.jksong files). Subfolders are fine. It starts with one
                demo song ("Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star", generated, public domain).
  Recordings\   What the recorder captures (lossless WAV files).
  Models\       The Studio's model files (about 3.8 GB). Only the Studio uses them;
                the player never does. They are already here, so the Studio works
                without downloading anything.
  Settings\     Empty on a fresh stick. The app keeps its settings, logs and
                self-check reports here, so nothing is written to the computer.
  Licenses\     The licence of @NAME@ (GPL-3.0-or-later) and of everything it uses.

  The app also creates Exports\ the first time you export a backing track.

Keep the folders together. They can sit at the top of the stick or together inside
one folder on it. Nothing depends on the drive letter.


2. Putting it on a USB stick
----------------------------

  a. Use a 32 GB (or larger) stick. Format it as exFAT, so that both Windows and the
     Mac can read and write it. Formatting erases everything on the stick.
       - On Windows: open File Explorer, right-click the stick, choose Format...,
         set File system to exFAT, set Allocation unit size to 32 kilobytes (the
         default on a 32 GB stick; on a bigger stick the default of 128 kilobytes
         wastes about 2 GB on the Studio's many small files), tick Quick Format,
         click Start.
       - On the Mac: open Disk Utility, select the stick, click Erase, choose
         Format: ExFAT and Scheme: Master Boot Record, click Erase. Disk Utility
         does not let you choose the allocation unit size, so format a stick
         bigger than 32 GB on Windows instead, as above.
  b. Copy everything inside this folder (the folders above and this file) onto the
     stick. Copy, do not move, so that you keep this folder as a spare.
     It is about @FILES@ files, most of them in Windows\Studio, so copying takes
     a while: roughly 5 to 30 minutes depending on the stick.
  c. When it is done, eject the stick before you pull it out (Windows: "Safely Remove
     Hardware"; Mac: the eject button in Finder). exFAT can lose data if a stick is
     pulled out while something is still being written.

  The same folder also works copied to an internal drive of a PC, which makes the
  Studio faster. Very deep folder paths can be too long for Windows: a folder such
  as C:\Users\<you>\Desktop\@NAME@ is fine.


3. First launch on Windows
--------------------------

  Double-click Windows\@NAME@.exe. Nothing needs to be installed on Windows 11.

  The app is not code-signed, so the first time Windows may show "Windows protected
  your PC". Click "More info", then "Run anyway".

  To make songs, open the Studio screen and drop audio or video files onto it. The
  first song on a new PC takes longer than the rest, because the graphics driver
  prepares its code once (it keeps that in Settings\cache, about 200 MB).


4. First launch on the Mac (MacBook Air, macOS 13 Ventura or later)
-------------------------------------------------------------------

  First put the Mac app into the Mac folder (see Mac\README.txt). Then open
  Mac\@NAME@.app from the stick in Finder.

  - A copy that came onto the stick from the Windows PC opens with a plain
    double-click.
  - A copy downloaded from the internet is blocked the first time, because it is not
    notarised by Apple. Do this once: in Finder, Control-click the app, choose Open,
    then click Open again. macOS is expected to ask: "macOS cannot verify the
    developer of "@NAME@". Are you sure you want to open it?" After that it opens
    normally.
  - The recorder needs the "Screen Recording" permission. macOS only lets apps hear
    the computer's sound through its screen-capture service, so that is what it
    asks for. @NAME@ records sound only and throws the picture away unseen. Allow it
    in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording, then quit and reopen
    the app.

  The Mac app has never been run on a real Mac yet. Please run the self-check (next
  section) the first time and bring its report back.


5. The self-check, and where its report goes
--------------------------------------------

  Click "Self-check" at the top right of the app. It starts at once: it plays a very
  quiet test tone, checks the output device, renders and changes the key of the demo
  song, and makes a three-second test recording. (Tick "Silent" and click "Run again"
  to check without any sound.)

  It writes a plain-text report into the Settings folder on the stick:

      Settings\selfcheck-<date and time>.txt

  Logs go to Settings\logs\. If something does not work, bring the stick back to the
  Windows PC with these files on it; they say what went wrong.

  On Windows the self-check can also run from a command prompt:
      Windows\@NAME@.exe --selfcheck --silent
  (exit code 0 means everything passed).


More: README.md, HANDOFF.md and docs\ in the project's source folder.
